ideas.working_title: Your Bank Says an $846 Purchase Is Pending. What Do You Do?
ideas.hook: An urgent bank text arrives with a link and phone number.
ideas.problem: Bank impersonation texts trick people into using the attacker's link or number.
ideas.safe_action: Open the bank's official app/site yourself and verify there.

ideas.working_title: You Owe an Unpaid Toll. Pay Now or Delete the Text?
ideas.hook: A $6.75 toll suddenly becomes a $50 late-fee threat.
ideas.problem: Small-dollar toll texts use urgency to trigger impulsive payment.
ideas.safe_action: Ignore the link and check the official toll authority directly.

ideas.working_title: Your Package Can't Be Delivered. Should You Pay the Redelivery Fee?
ideas.hook: You're expecting a package when a delivery problem text arrives.
ideas.problem: Smishing exploits real package expectations to steal payment or identity data.
ideas.safe_action: Track the parcel only through the carrier's official site/app.

ideas.working_title: A Friend on WhatsApp Asks for Your 6-Digit Code. Send It?
ideas.hook: A known contact says a code was sent to you by mistake.
ideas.problem: Account-takeover scams trick users into surrendering verification codes.
ideas.safe_action: Never share login or verification codes; contact the friend another way.

ideas.working_title: You're Pumping Gas. Is Your Purse Safe on the Passenger Seat?
ideas.hook: You turn toward the pump for 20 seconds.
ideas.problem: Parking-lot 'slider' thieves exploit unlocked doors and distraction.
ideas.safe_action: Lock the vehicle while fueling and keep valuables with you/out of sight.

ideas.working_title: ATM Card Skimmer: Can You Spot It Before You Insert Your Card?
ideas.hook: The ATM looks normal — except one piece moves.
ideas.problem: Skimmers and overlays capture card data and PINs.
ideas.safe_action: Inspect readers/keypads, cover your PIN, and use safer indoor ATMs when possible.

ideas.working_title: Your Amazon Package Says Delivered — Then It Disappears.
ideas.hook: The delivery photo is there, but the box isn't.
ideas.problem: Porch piracy targets packages left unattended after delivery.
ideas.safe_action: Use prompt pickup, lockers/hold-for-pickup, trusted neighbors, or signature for valuables.

ideas.working_title: Your Daughter Calls Crying: 'Mom, I Need Money Now.' Is It Really Her?
ideas.hook: A familiar voice begs for emergency money.
ideas.problem: AI voice cloning and impersonation exploit family panic.
ideas.safe_action: Hang up and call the person back on a known number; use a family safe word.

ideas.working_title: WhatsApp Job Offer: Earn $300 a Day 'Optimizing Products.' Scam or Job?
ideas.hook: A stranger offers easy work and instant commissions.
ideas.problem: Task scams show fake earnings, then demand deposits to unlock them.
ideas.safe_action: Never pay to get paid; ignore unexpected task-job messages.

ideas.working_title: Can Someone Steal Your Tap-to-Pay Card Just by Standing Near You?
ideas.hook: A stranger gets close to your wallet in a crowded place.
ideas.problem: Viral RFID fears can distract from more common card-fraud risks.
ideas.safe_action: Explain the short tap range and focus on real defenses: alerts, card control, secure readers, quick reporting.

ideas.working_title: Gas Pump Skimmer: Swipe, Insert, or Tap?
ideas.hook: You're paying at a pump late at night.
ideas.problem: Fuel-pump skimmers can capture card data; some are hidden internally.
ideas.safe_action: Prefer tap when available, inspect the terminal, run debit as credit, or pay inside.

ideas.working_title: Your Phone Suddenly Has No Service. Could Someone Be Stealing Your Number?
ideas.hook: No calls. No texts. Then a carrier notification appears.
ideas.problem: SIM-swap/port-out fraud can hijack phone numbers and text-based MFA.
ideas.safe_action: Contact the carrier immediately, use an account PIN, and prefer authenticator/security-key MFA for sensitive accounts.

ideas.working_title: WhatsApp Investment Group Full of 'Winners' — Who Are These People?
ideas.hook: Everyone in the group seems to be making money.
ideas.problem: Scammers create fake investment groups and testimonials to manufacture trust.
ideas.safe_action: Never invest based on chat-group claims; independently verify firms and advisors.

ideas.working_title: A 'Wrong Number' Text Turns Friendly. Why Keep Talking?
ideas.hook: A stranger apologizes for texting the wrong person, then starts a friendship.
ideas.problem: Relationship-building can be the opening move for investment or romance fraud.
ideas.safe_action: Stop engaging with unsolicited strangers who pivot toward money or investment.

ideas.working_title: Your WhatsApp Group Admin Says 'Scan This QR Code to Stay in the Group.'
ideas.hook: A familiar group suddenly asks members to scan a QR code.
ideas.problem: QR/device-linking and phishing tricks can hand attackers access or credentials.
ideas.safe_action: Verify admin requests separately and never scan unexpected login/device-link QR codes.

ideas.working_title: Your Friend's WhatsApp Asks for Money — But Their Account Was Hacked.
ideas.hook: The message sounds exactly like your friend.
ideas.problem: Compromised accounts inherit trust and can solicit emergency payments.
ideas.safe_action: Call the friend on a known number before sending money.

ideas.working_title: Why 'Move This Chat to WhatsApp' Can Be a Red Flag.
ideas.hook: A marketplace seller or new contact wants to leave the platform immediately.
ideas.problem: Moving off-platform can remove platform protections and make impersonation/payment scams easier.
ideas.safe_action: Keep marketplace transactions and support inside the platform until identity/payment is verified.

ideas.working_title: A WhatsApp 'Customer Service Agent' Wants Remote Access to Your Phone.
ideas.hook: Support says they need screen-sharing or remote access.
ideas.problem: Fake support agents use remote access to steal credentials and approve transfers.
ideas.safe_action: End the chat and use the company's official support channel.

ideas.working_title: Chip Card 'Shimmer' vs Skimmer: What Can You Actually Check?
ideas.hook: Your card reader feels normal — but fraud appears later.
ideas.problem: Some devices sit inside readers, making visual detection difficult.
ideas.safe_action: Use trusted terminals, tap when available, enable alerts, and report suspicious transactions fast.

ideas.working_title: Before You Enter Your PIN, Do This With Your Other Hand.
ideas.hook: A hidden camera may be watching the keypad.
ideas.problem: Skimming setups often pair card capture with PIN capture.
ideas.safe_action: Cover the keypad completely while entering the PIN.

ideas.working_title: Small $1 Charge on Your Card? Don't Ignore It.
ideas.hook: A tiny unfamiliar transaction appears.
ideas.problem: Small test charges can precede larger unauthorized activity.
ideas.safe_action: Lock the card if needed and contact the issuer promptly about unfamiliar charges.

ideas.working_title: RFID-Blocking Wallet: Essential Security or Mostly Peace of Mind?
ideas.hook: A product promises to stop criminals reading your cards from across the room.
ideas.problem: Fear-based claims can overstate practical contactless-card proximity risk.
ideas.safe_action: Explain realistic range/transaction controls and prioritize account alerts and secure use.

ideas.working_title: Restaurant Takes Your Card Out of Sight. What Should You Watch For?
ideas.hook: Your card disappears behind the counter for several minutes.
ideas.problem: Card data can be copied or misused when physical control is lost.
ideas.safe_action: Use tap/chip at the table when available and monitor alerts/transactions.

ideas.working_title: Cashier Says the Tap Failed — 'Just Swipe It.' Any Risk?
ideas.hook: The terminal pushes you toward the magnetic stripe.
ideas.problem: Magnetic-stripe data is more vulnerable to skimming than tap/chip.
ideas.safe_action: If the reader looks suspicious, use another terminal or payment method.

ideas.working_title: You Get 12 MFA Prompts You Didn't Request. Approve One to Make Them Stop?
ideas.hook: Your phone keeps buzzing with login approvals.
ideas.problem: MFA fatigue attacks rely on accidental or frustrated approval.
ideas.safe_action: Deny every unknown prompt, change the password, and review active sessions.

ideas.working_title: One Password for Everything? Here's the Chain Reaction After One Breach.
ideas.hook: One leaked password unlocks several accounts.
ideas.problem: Credential stuffing exploits password reuse across services.
ideas.safe_action: Use unique passwords and a password manager; enable MFA.

ideas.working_title: Your Email Password Was Changed and Recovery Info Looks Different.
ideas.hook: You're suddenly locked out of your email.
ideas.problem: Email takeover can unlock banking, shopping, and social accounts via password resets.
ideas.safe_action: Recover email first, revoke sessions, change linked passwords, and check recovery settings.

ideas.working_title: Hotel Wi-Fi Has Two Networks With Almost the Same Name. Which One Is Real?
ideas.hook: Two nearly identical Wi-Fi names appear.
ideas.problem: Fake or malicious networks can imitate legitimate public Wi-Fi.
ideas.safe_action: Ask staff for the exact network; avoid sensitive transactions on unknown networks; use HTTPS/VPN as appropriate.

ideas.working_title: Data Breach Notice Arrives. What Should You Do Today — Not Next Month?
ideas.hook: A company says your data may have been exposed.
ideas.problem: Delays can give criminals time to exploit stolen credentials or identity data.
ideas.safe_action: Change exposed passwords, enable MFA, monitor accounts/credit, and follow breach-specific steps.

ideas.working_title: A Password Reset Email You Didn't Request: Delete It or Investigate?
ideas.hook: A reset message appears without you doing anything.
ideas.problem: It may signal an attempted takeover or be phishing itself.
ideas.safe_action: Don't use the email link; open the service directly and review security activity.

ideas.working_title: Your CEO Appears on Video Asking for a Secret Wire Transfer. Real?
ideas.hook: A familiar executive appears on a video call with an urgent request.
ideas.problem: Deepfake audio/video can strengthen business impersonation.
ideas.safe_action: Verify high-risk money requests through a second known channel and established approval process.

ideas.working_title: Celebrity Deepfake Says 'Double Your Crypto Today.'
ideas.hook: A famous face appears to endorse an investment.
ideas.problem: AI-generated promotional videos can lend false credibility to fraud.
ideas.safe_action: Verify through official channels and never trust investment claims based on celebrity videos.

ideas.working_title: Police Caller ID Says You Missed Jury Duty. Pay the Fine Now?
ideas.hook: Caller ID shows the local sheriff.
ideas.problem: Scammers spoof law-enforcement numbers and threaten arrest to force payment.
ideas.safe_action: Hang up and call the agency using an independently found official number.

ideas.working_title: The 'FBI' Says It Recovered Your Scam Money — Just Pay a Release Fee.
ideas.hook: After losing money, someone promises to recover it.
ideas.problem: Recovery scammers target victims a second time, sometimes impersonating authorities.
ideas.safe_action: Do not pay recovery fees; contact IC3/FTC only through official sites you navigate to yourself.

ideas.working_title: Create a Family Safe Word Before the Emergency Call Comes.
ideas.hook: A panicked voice can be convincing even when fake.
ideas.problem: AI voice impersonation exploits urgency and emotional familiarity.
ideas.safe_action: Agree on a private family verification word and a callback rule.

ideas.working_title: Can You Reliably 'Hear' an AI Voice? Don't Bet Your Money on It.
ideas.hook: The voice sounds almost perfect.
ideas.problem: AI voice clues are becoming unreliable as a sole defense.
ideas.safe_action: Use independent identity verification, not audio quality, before sending money or secrets.

ideas.working_title: You Put Your Laptop in the Trunk After Parking. Too Late?
ideas.hook: You arrive, then visibly move valuables to the trunk.
ideas.problem: A thief watching the lot may already know what's in the vehicle.
ideas.safe_action: Hide/remove valuables before reaching the destination.

ideas.working_title: Parking Lot Rule: Nothing Valuable Visible — Not Even a Charging Cable.
ideas.hook: A cable or bag hints that electronics may be nearby.
ideas.problem: Visible clues can make a vehicle a more attractive break-in target.
ideas.safe_action: Take valuables with you and leave the cabin visibly empty.

ideas.working_title: Someone Drops Coins Near Your Car and Asks for Help. Where's Your Bag?
ideas.hook: A stranger creates a small distraction while you're loading the car.
ideas.problem: Distraction theft separates attention from valuables.
ideas.safe_action: Keep doors locked and valuables controlled before engaging with strangers.

ideas.working_title: QR Code on a Parking Meter: Official Sticker or Fake Payment Trap?
ideas.hook: A QR sticker sits over the meter's normal instructions.
ideas.problem: Tampered QR codes can redirect payment to phishing sites.
ideas.safe_action: Use the official parking app/site or type the address yourself; inspect stickers for tampering.

ideas.working_title: At the Gas Station, Lock the Passenger Door Before You Start Pumping.
ideas.hook: Your attention is outside the car.
ideas.problem: Unlocked doors create an easy opportunity for slider theft.
ideas.safe_action: Lock doors, keep keys/phone with you, and stay aware.

ideas.working_title: You See Broken Glass Beside a Parking Spot. Park There Anyway?
ideas.hook: The spot is convenient, but the ground tells a story.
ideas.problem: Environmental clues can indicate repeated vehicle break-ins.
ideas.safe_action: Choose a visible, well-lit area and remove valuables.

ideas.working_title: Package Arriving While You're at Work? Don't Let It Sit All Day.
ideas.hook: A delivery lands hours before you get home.
ideas.problem: Unattended packages create opportunity for porch theft.
ideas.safe_action: Use lockers, hold-for-pickup, delivery alerts, neighbors, or signature for valuable items.

ideas.working_title: Unexpected Package With a QR Code Inside: Scan to See Who Sent It?
ideas.hook: A random package arrives with a mystery QR card.
ideas.problem: Brushing scams can pair unexpected packages with phishing QR codes.
ideas.safe_action: Do not scan unknown QR codes; secure shopping accounts and report suspicious packages.

ideas.working_title: A New Credit Card Never Arrived. Wait Another Week?
ideas.hook: A valuable piece of mail is overdue.
ideas.problem: Mail theft can expose cards and identity information.
ideas.safe_action: Contact the issuer/sender promptly and monitor accounts.

ideas.working_title: Going Out of Town? Don't Leave Mail and Packages Advertising It.
ideas.hook: Mail piles up for days.
ideas.problem: Accumulated mail signals absence and increases theft exposure.
ideas.safe_action: Use hold-mail/hold-for-pickup or trusted pickup arrangements.

ideas.working_title: Package Photo Shows 'Delivered' — But Is the Photo Enough?
ideas.hook: A delivery photo confirms placement, not continued possession.
ideas.problem: Consumers may assume a photo guarantees the package stayed secure.
ideas.safe_action: Retrieve quickly and use secure delivery options for high-value items.

ideas.working_title: Someone Offers to 'Redeliver' Your Stolen Package for a Fee.
ideas.hook: A thief or fake support contact claims they can fix the loss.
ideas.problem: Secondary scams exploit the stress of missing deliveries.
ideas.safe_action: Work only through the retailer/carrier's official support path.

ideas.working_title: Facebook Marketplace Buyer Sends a Payment Screenshot. Is That Money Real?
ideas.hook: A screenshot says 'payment sent' but your account shows nothing.
ideas.problem: Fake payment confirmations pressure sellers to release goods.
ideas.safe_action: Trust only money confirmed inside your own account/app.

ideas.working_title: Buyer 'Accidentally' Overpaid. Send the Difference Back?
ideas.hook: A payment or check is larger than agreed.
ideas.problem: Overpayment scams use fake/reversible funds to make victims send real money back.
ideas.safe_action: Never refund an overpayment outside the original verified transaction process.

ideas.working_title: This Rental Is $600 Cheaper Than Everything Else. Deal or Scam?
ideas.hook: A perfect rental appears far below market.
ideas.problem: Fake listings use urgency and deposits to steal money before tours or verification.
ideas.safe_action: Verify ownership/listing, see the property, and never rush deposits to strangers.

ideas.working_title: Instagram Ad Has 80% Off a Famous Brand. Click or Search?
ideas.hook: A polished ad promises a huge discount.
ideas.problem: Social shopping scams lead to fake storefronts, non-delivery, or counterfeit goods.
ideas.safe_action: Search for the retailer independently and pay by a protected method.

ideas.working_title: Hotel Texts: 'Your Reservation Failed — Update Card Here.'
ideas.hook: The message knows your travel dates.
ideas.problem: Imposter messages can exploit leaked or scraped reservation details.
ideas.safe_action: Open the hotel/booking app directly or call the official number.

ideas.working_title: Amazon 'Refund Department' Calls You About a $1,499 Order.
ideas.hook: A caller says a huge order was placed on your account.
ideas.problem: Retailer impersonation creates panic to extract credentials, remote access, or payments.
ideas.safe_action: Hang up and check your order history in the official app/site.

ideas.working_title: Recruiter Texts: '$42 an Hour, Start Today.' What Do You Verify First?
ideas.hook: A high-paying remote job appears by text.
ideas.problem: Job scams collect identity data, fake-check payments, or upfront fees.
ideas.safe_action: Verify the employer through its official careers site; never pay to get hired.

ideas.working_title: Your Online Friend Shows Huge Crypto Profits and Offers to Teach You.
ideas.hook: Someone you trust online offers a 'safe' investment system.
ideas.problem: Romance/confidence scams often pivot into cryptocurrency investment fraud.
ideas.safe_action: Never send money to an online-only relationship for investment; independently verify investments.

ideas.working_title: Investment App Shows You Made $18,000 — Why Can't You Withdraw?
ideas.hook: Your balance looks amazing, but withdrawal requires another fee.
ideas.problem: Fake investment platforms display fabricated profits and demand more money.
ideas.safe_action: Stop sending funds; document evidence and report promptly.

ideas.working_title: Never Pay Money to Unlock Your 'Earnings.'
ideas.hook: A job platform asks you to deposit money before withdrawing wages.
ideas.problem: Task scams reverse the normal employer-worker payment flow.
ideas.safe_action: If you must pay to get paid, stop — it's a major scam signal.

ideas.working_title: WhatsApp Stock 'Professor' + Assistant + VIP Group: Why So Many People?
ideas.hook: A polished group has a professor, assistant, and cheering members.
ideas.problem: Coordinated personas and fake testimonials manufacture authority and social proof.
ideas.safe_action: Verify advisers/firm registrations independently and never wire/crypto funds based on chat-group instructions.

ideas.working_title: Lost Money to Crypto? Beware the Person Promising to Recover It.
ideas.hook: A 'recovery expert' says your stolen crypto was found.
ideas.problem: Recovery scams revictimize people who already lost money.
ideas.safe_action: Do not pay recovery fees; report through official law-enforcement/consumer channels.
